title: Guarding the tongue against sin
english: I said, “I will guard my ways so that I do not sin with my tongue.” I set a guard on my mouth when the sinner stood against me. I was silenced and I was humbled (Psalm 39:1, LXX 38:2).
translator_notes: Copy-text PG 12 (Migne) Rufinus Latin via Archive PDF pdftotext; no first-edition GCS.
True OET: no ANF; do not copy Trigg FOTC / Prinzivalli SC / Perrone 2015.
After tip 091b5ed2; Psalms Rufinus Homilia I in Ps 38 CLOSEOUT.
orientation: The psalmist speaks in the first person, resolving to guard his ways and his mouth while a sinner stands against him.

title: The heart burns in meditation and asks to know its end
english: My heart grew hot within me; in my meditation a fire will blaze up (Psalm 39:3). Make known to me, Lord, my end (Psalm 39:4). Glory to Christ. Amen.
translator_notes: Copy-text PG 12 (Migne) Rufinus Latin via Archive PDF pdftotext; no first-edition GCS.
True OET: no ANF; do not copy Trigg FOTC / Prinzivalli SC / Perrone 2015.
After tip 091b5ed2; Psalms Rufinus Homilia I in Ps 38 CLOSEOUT.
orientation: The psalmist, having just said he was silent and humbled, now speaks of his burning heart and asks the Lord to make known his end; Origen closes the section with a doxology to Christ.
